interpretations: Count every invoice with a matching order and customer, group by `Customers.gender` including `NULL` as a group, and average shares over groups with at least one invoice.
Count every invoice with a matching order and customer, exclude customers whose gender is `NULL`, and average shares over the remaining groups with at least one invoice.
Count every invoice with a matching order and customer, include recorded gender values with zero invoices when averaging shares, and include `NULL` as a group if present among customers.
Count every invoice with a matching order and customer, include recorded non-`NULL` gender values with zero invoices when averaging shares, and exclude customers whose gender is `NULL`.
In each interpretation, return only groups whose share strictly exceeds the average, with the gender, invoice count, unrounded share, and unrounded difference from the average.
queries:
WITH gender_counts AS (
  SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count
  FROM Invoices AS i
  JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
  JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.gender
)
SELECT AVG(1.0 * invoice_count / (SELECT SUM(invoice_count) FROM gender_counts)) AS average_share
FROM gender_counts

WITH gender_invoice_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count
    FROM Invoices AS i
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c.gender
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
),
invoice_shares AS (
    SELECT invoice_count * 1.0 / SUM(invoice_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM gender_invoice_counts
)
SELECT AVG(share) AS average_share
FROM invoice_shares

WITH gender_invoice_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(i.invoice_number) AS invoice_count
    FROM Customers AS c
    LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
)
SELECT AVG(
    1.0 * invoice_count /
    NULLIF((SELECT SUM(invoice_count) FROM gender_invoice_counts), 0)
) AS average_invoice_share
FROM gender_invoice_counts

WITH invoice_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(i.invoice_number) AS invoice_count
    FROM Customers AS c
    LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c.gender
)
SELECT AVG(1.0 * invoice_count / NULLIF(total_invoices, 0)) AS average_share
FROM invoice_counts
CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT SUM(invoice_count) AS total_invoices
    FROM invoice_counts
)

WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count
    FROM Invoices AS i
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
),
gender_shares AS (
    SELECT
        gender,
        invoice_count,
        1.0 * invoice_count / SUM(invoice_count) OVER () AS share
    FROM gender_counts
),
compared AS (
    SELECT
        gender,
        invoice_count,
        share,
        share - AVG(share) OVER () AS difference_from_average
    FROM gender_shares
)
SELECT gender, invoice_count, share, difference_from_average
FROM compared
WHERE difference_from_average > 0;
